# Vaccine Temperature Compliance Review

Date: 2025-02-24  
Attendees: Saskia Fennmoor, Tobiah Ulmford  

**Agenda:**  
- Review of temperature deviations in January vaccine shipments  
- Assessment of current sensor tag performance  
- Updates to cold-storage protocols  

**Discussion:**  
Saskia reported that 7 out of 120 shipments last month experienced temperature excursions exceeding the 2°C–8°C range, with 5 of these occurring during last-mile delivery. The average duration of excursions was 38 minutes, up from 22 minutes in December. Tobiah noted that the current sensor tags, model TempTrack-5, have a battery life of 72 hours, which is approaching expiration for some units on longer routes. He suggested exploring tags with at least 120-hour battery capacity for improved reliability. Both agreed that alerts were sometimes delayed due to intermittent network coverage in rural zones.  

**Decisions:**  
- Increase minimum sensor tag battery life requirement to 120 hours starting March 1  
- Implement secondary cold-storage checks at distribution hubs to catch deviations earlier  
- Pilot low-power wide-area network (LPWAN) connectivity in the North Bay delivery region to improve real-time alerting  

**Action Items:**  
- Tobiah to source and test extended-life sensor tags by 2025-03-10  
- Saskia to revise cold-storage SOPs incorporating dual checkpoint protocol by 2025-02-28  
- Tobiah to coordinate LPWAN pilot setup with network provider by 2025-03-15
